title: Eagles linemen Ojomo, Johnson fight at camp
dek: Defensive tackle Moro Ojomo and offensive tackle Fred Johnson fought during team drills on the 11th day of Eagles training camp. Punches and a diving tackle followed before coaches separated them. The incident occurred the day before the team's preseason opener.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: The altercation happened during the final practice before the Eagles' preseason game against Baltimore.
bottom_line: Team management met with both players individually post-practice and halted competitive drills to reset. Watch for any disciplinary statements from the Eagles or changes to lineup decisions ahead of the Ravens game, and whether either player appears on an injury report.
body: Defensive tackle Moro Ojomo and offensive tackle Fred Johnson fought during team drills on the 11th day of Eagles training camp, according to ESPN's reporting. The incident occurred Thursday, the final practice before the Eagles' preseason opener against the Baltimore Ravens.

Ojomo took exception to a late shove by Johnson and squared up, ready to fight. Coaches kept both players in for the next play after the initial confrontation. When Johnson blocked Ojomo to the ground and landed on him with his full weight, punches were thrown between the two. Ojomo dove at Johnson's knees after finding his way through the crowd, bringing the 6-foot-7, 326-pound Johnson to the ground before coaches separated them.

The intensity halted team drills. After a group huddle to reset, the Eagles finished with a less competitive developmental period instead of continuing against-the-grain competition. General manager Howie Roseman, coach Nick Sirianni, and chief security officer Dom DiSardo gathered around Johnson to help calm him down.

Roseman met with Ojomo before talking with Johnson post-practice for about five minutes as the offensive lineman sat on blocking pads. Sirianni had framed the day before practice as an opportunity for the team's competitive edge: "I'm just so excited to see all the guys compete. At the end of the day, this business is for people that are ultracompetitive. And it's always good to go against somebody else. Sometimes at this point of camp, you're like, 'Man, I just want to hit somebody else and go against somebody else.'" according to ESPN.
The brief does not confirm whether either player was injured in the altercation or whether any disciplinary action was taken by the team following the incident.
